Topic: The Central Limit Theorem (CLT): The Bridge to Normalcy

Target audience: University students (Introductory Statistics)

Section: section_1 — The Hook: The Chaos of Individuality

Lecture lines:
Individual data points are often wildly chaotic.
Different distributions show unique, messy patterns.
We calculate sample means to find stability.

Planned animations:
Create 500 scattered dots (#FF5733) representing chaotic individual data.
Display text 'Data Points' (#FFFFFF) near the scattered dots.
Animate dots drifting randomly across the black screen.

Section: section_2 — The Experiment: From Chaos to Order

Lecture lines:
Take multiple random samples from a population.
Calculate the mean for each group.
Plot these means on a new graph.

Planned animations:
Create a central vertical axis (#FFFFFF) labeled 'Mean'.
Animate dots moving toward the vertical axis over time.
Show dots settling into a heap structure forming a shape.

Section: section_3 — The Big Reveal: The Normal Distribution

Lecture lines:
Populations can be any random shape.
Sample means form a normal distribution.
The bell curve stabilizes with larger samples.
The center matches the population mean.
It's the CLT bridging chaos to order.

Planned animations:
Outline a bell-shaped curve (#4287f5) over the settled dots.
Highlight the peak of the curve with a yellow line (#FFFF00).
Display text 'Normal Distribution' (#FFFFFF) above the curve.
Fade out individual dots leaving only the bell curve.
Pulse the curve (#4287f5) to emphasize its symmetry.

Section: section_4 — Key Conditions for Validity

Lecture lines:
Samples must be independent and random.
Use a sample size of thirty or more.
These conditions guarantee a normal curve.

Planned animations:
Display text 'Independent Trials' (#00FF00) on the screen.
Display text 'Large Sample Size' (#00FF00) below the first text.
Show checkmarks (#FFFF00) appearing next to both conditions.

Section: section_5 — The 'Why It Matters' Application

Lecture lines:
CLT lets us infer population properties.
We predict vast outcomes from small samples.
This saves time, effort, and resources.

Planned animations:
Show a factory assembly line with consistent outputs (#FF5733).
Overlay a normal curve (#4287f5) representing consistent quality control.
Highlight the standard deviation area (#FFFF00) under the curve.

        # BASE

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Create chaotic data points

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.play(Write(label))
